content.text: I reviewed the shipped files, recomputed every expected value, and tested plausible wrong analyses against each tolerance before answering.

outside_claim.reason: S28's saturated-loading-control pitfall and S22/S24's 'loading control bands are appropriate (not saturated)' check are exactly what a dilution series answers; the job supplies the arithmetic so a subject reading the sections cannot defensibly answer otherwise.

gives_away.reason: The job is symmetric over GAPDH and MDM2 and never says which antibody saturates; the rule it states (slope from the lowest load, 15 percent allowance) is not a rule the sections supply - S28's only saturation criterion is pixel-based (max pixel < 90% of detector range), which is inapplicable to a density table, so this belongs in criterion_given.

repeats.reason: No other task uses a load-response series or asks about proportionality to input.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed from the shipped bytes: slope 4993.6/ug; at 2.5/5/10 ug the ratios are 1.012/0.991/0.993 (inside 15%), at 20 ug 57313.2 against a predicted 99872 (43% low) and at 40 ug worse, so 10.0 and true; MDM2 is within 1% of its low-load slope at every point, so 40.0 and false. The Eaton quotes fairly state that saturation occurs within a load series and that a linear working range can span a wide load range.

wrong_passes.reason: The two booleans must split, so a constant answer fails; a 10% or 20% allowance returns the same two loads (the GAPDH deviation jumps from 1% to 43% between adjacent steps), and taking the slope from an all-points fit instead disqualifies every load and fails. I could not name an analysis that errs and still passes all four fields.

g1_dilution_series_linearity.criterion_given: Take the proportionality constant from the lowest load, allow 15 percent deviation, report the largest qualifying load.

outside_claim.reason: S28/S29.2 tell the analyst to check whether a housekeeping protein responds to the treatment and to prefer a total-protein stain; that is precisely what the job asks.

gives_away.reason: The job never says which housekeeping protein moves, and it does not state which denominator to use for the LDHA folds; the per-total-protein phrasing appears only inside the definitions of the two diagnostic booleans.

repeats.reason: No other task asks whether a reference protein is itself treatment-responsive.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: GAPDH per total protein falls from 0.05451 to 0.03265 (40% change, true); ACTB holds at 0.0583 vs 0.0581 (false); LDHA per total protein gives mean folds 1.8920 and 2.5840, matching the planted values.

wrong_passes.reason: Reporting raw LDHA ratios with no normalization at all - the claim's own flagship pitfall ('Never plot raw intensities as a quantitative result') - gives mean 1.9021 for 24h and 2.5476 for 48h against expected 1.8920 and 2.5840, i.e. 0.5% and 1.4% off, comfortably inside the 8 percent band, while the two booleans are computed exactly as the job dictates. The per-lane loading factor is only +/-8% and averages out over three repeats, so the task does not bite on an omitted normalization.

g2_treatment_responsive_control.criterion_given: More than 15 percent change per unit total protein between Hypoxia_48h and Normoxia counts as treatment-responsive.
g2_treatment_responsive_control.replacement: Keep the same three-repeat hypoxia panel but make the per-lane loading factor large and condition-correlated (for example Hypoxia lanes loaded roughly 1.4x heavier than Normoxia), and ask only for the amount of LDHA relative to Normoxia plus a judgment on each candidate reference, without the job specifying any per-total-protein quantity. Then the GAPDH-normalized answer, the ACTB/total-protein answer and the unnormalized answer all separate, so both the 'wrong reference' and the 'no reference' errors fail while the prescribed total-protein route passes.

outside_claim.reason: S23 tells the analyst to apply background subtraction using a local measurement near each band, and S28/S29.1 forbid reporting raw densities; the job asks for exactly the corrected, loading-normalized comparison and whether the raw comparison disagrees.

gives_away.reason: The sentence about the stain mark restates a value already visible in the local_background_per_px column (8.0 vs 2.0) and reveals no output: the job does not say which protein's raw comparison is misleading, does not say to normalize to GAPDH, and asks the disagreement question symmetrically for both proteins. The discriminating judgments - multiply background by band area, divide by the loading control - remain the subject's.

repeats.reason: It is the only task with a per-pixel background term and band areas, and the only two-lane single-blot case.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: corrected CDKN1A 11986.1/26656.5 = 0.44965 (Control) and 23829.4/67618.3 = 0.35241 (Treated), fold 0.78374; CCND1 fold 1.99070; raw CDKN1A rises 1.336x while the corrected fold falls, so disagree is true, and CCND1 rises on both readings, so false. All match the planted values; the Degasperi quotes state the per-band background removal and the per-lane normalization the outputs rest on.

wrong_passes.reason: Skipping the background term entirely gives 0.9192 and 1.7577 (expected bands 0.737-0.831 and 1.871-2.110) - both fail; subtracting the per-pixel value without area scaling gives essentially the same 0.919 and fails; skipping the loading control after correct background subtraction gives 1.988 for CDKN1A and fails and also flips its boolean. I could not name a wrong route that passes.

outside_claim.reason: S20 (bands not detected), S24 ('loading control bands present and measurable for all samples', 'all repetitions included') and S28's documentation pitfall all cover noticing and reporting an incomplete repeat rather than quantifying around it.

gives_away.reason: The field is defined with an explicit 'none if every repeat is complete' escape and no row, repeat or protein is named; the subject must find R3 and establish that the loading-control rows are all present.

repeats.reason: It is the only task where a measurement is absent from the file.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: R3 lacks Treated BAX, every GAPDH row is present, and the normalized folds for R1/R2/R4 are 2.0757, 2.4689 and 1.8278, mean 2.1242, with n=3 - all as planted.

wrong_passes.reason: Dropping the GAPDH normalization and averaging raw BAX Treated/Control ratios gives 2.1239, 2.3073 and 1.7832, mean 2.0715 - only 2.5% from the expected 2.1242 and inside the 6 percent band - while the four structural fields (R3, false, true, 3.0) are unaffected. The named pitfall 'reporting raw band intensities without loading-control normalization' therefore passes this task; the tolerance_basis considers only zero-imputation (1.59), not this route.

g4_incomplete_replicate.replacement: Keep the same four-repeat structure with R3's Treated BAX band absent, but make the per-lane loading systematically unequal between Control and Treated (for example Treated lanes carrying roughly 1.5x the load across repeats) so that the unnormalized mean fold lands far outside the tolerance while the GAPDH-normalized mean remains the expected value. The missing-band fields are unchanged and the task then bites on both the undetected band and the omitted normalization.

outside_claim.reason: S28 names this pitfall and S29 the remedy; the quantity asked for is within the claim.

gives_away.reason: The job spells out S28's prescribed order of steps verbatim in substance - 'computing the Treated-to-Control ratio inside each experiment and then averaging those three ratios' - and assigns it to the primary output field, and it announces that aggregation order is the issue under test by naming both procedures. The judgment the claim asserts (normalize within each replicate first, then aggregate) is handed to the subject, leaving only arithmetic; the 10 percent cut-off is additionally supplied.

repeats.reason: No other task contrasts two orders of aggregation.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: STAT3 per-repeat ratios 3.1602, 2.0157, 1.3498, mean 2.1752; pooling first gives 2.3514/1.3495 = 1.7424, 19.9% away, so true. TUBB ratios 1.7498, 1.8562, 1.8115, mean 1.8058; pooled 1.8147, 0.5% away, so false. All match the planted values.

wrong_passes.reason: Pooling first fails STAT3 (1.742 against a 2.045-2.306 band) and flips nothing else into agreement; the geometric mean of the ratios (2.049) is a defensible alternative rather than an error, and it sits at the edge of the band.

g5_aggregation_order.criterion_given: A disagreement of more than 10 percent between the two orders counts as the order mattering.
g5_aggregation_order.replacement: Ship the same three-membrane, two-protein file but ask only for the treatment effect on each protein (one fold per protein) and for a flag on whether the per-membrane scales make the experiments poolable, without naming or describing either aggregation procedure. Set the tolerance so that the pooled-first answer fails for STAT3 and both routes pass for TUBB; the subject then has to supply the order of operations from the claim rather than execute one the job dictated.

outside_claim.reason: S21 names large standard deviations between repetitions and conditional outlier exclusion, and S28/S29.4 require documenting rather than silently dropping; the job asks for the spread, the discrepant repeat and both analyses.

gives_away.reason: Neither the discrepant repeat nor which protein is variable is named, and the CV cut-off is not a threshold the sections state. Asking for both means is the sections' reporting remedy, but the detection work (which protein is variable, which repeat is discrepant) is left to the subject.

repeats.reason: It is the only task turning on inter-replicate spread; g4's defect is an absent row, not variability.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: CASP3 ratios 2.1811, 1.9322, 2.2403, 9.1749, 2.0428; CV 0.90 (true), median 2.1811 so R4 is furthest, mean all 3.5142, mean excluding 2.0991. HSP90 ratios 1.4419-1.6012, CV 0.04 (false). All planted values reproduce. The attached Eaton quotes are generic, but each of these outputs is fully defined computationally by the job, so no output depends on the quote to be determinate.

wrong_passes.reason: The two CV booleans must split; a population standard deviation gives CV 0.81, still true, and leaves everything else unchanged (not an error that passes while being wrong about anything scored); the two means differ by 40 percent, so neither can stand in for the other, and naming any repeat other than R4 fails.

g6_variable_repeat.criterion_given: A coefficient of variation above 0.5 counts as high variability.

findings: Criterion 1 (expected values right and skill-independent): I recomputed every output from the shipped bytes and all 26 planted values reproduce exactly - g1's 10.0/40.0 and the split booleans, g2's 1.8920/2.5840 with GAPDH down 40% per unit total protein and ACTB flat, g3's 0.78374/1.99070 with CDKN1A's raw comparison inverted, g4's R3/false/true/3.0/2.1242, g5's 2.1752/1.8058 with a 19.9% order effect for STAT3 and 0.5% for TUBB, and g6's CV 0.90/0.04, R4, 3.5142/2.0991. The generator implements the quoted Degasperi model (divide by a reference measured in the same sample) and nothing from the skill; every threshold used for scoring is stated in the job, not taken from the skill's text, and the reference solver derives each value from the files rather than reading arguments. Two weaknesses: several boolean and text outputs carry decorative quotes - one Eaton sentence about loading standards underwrites g4's undetected band, g6's CV flag and g6's discrepant repeat alike - so for those fields the rule actually in force is the job's arithmetic definition, not the published sentence; this does not make any value wrong but it thins the 'independent rule' story the justification tells.

Criterion 2 (exercising the claim as a whole): tested - saturated loading control (g1), treatment-responsive housekeeping protein (g2), raw/background-contaminated densities (g3), undetected band and incomplete repeat (g4), aggregation before fold change (g5), high inter-replicate variability and exclusion reporting (g6); each pairs its defect with a clean counterpart in the same file and each boolean pair must split, which is a real strength. Untested: naming any prescribed remedy (re-image, dilute, repeat the transfer, switch to a total-protein stain) although expected_behavior makes that half the behavior; the skill's own saturation criterion (max pixel < 90% of detector range, S28), which cannot be applied to a density table at all; ROI placement, grid-overlay verification and per-image threshold tuning (S20, S28, S29.3); stating SD vs SE and n (S24, S28, S29.5); drawing conclusions from n = 1 or 2 (S28); preserving intermediates and cross-checking the chart against the blot (S29.6-.7). Eaton bears on saturation and on housekeeping instability, so those gaps are covered by references; nothing in references or in python_checked.search_record bears on remedies, error-bar labelling or ROI work, and the record shows zero searches run for this claim in this attempt.

Criterion 3 (fair and searching comparison): g1, g3 and g6 bite properly - g3 in particular now rejects both the omitted background term (0.9192 and 1.7577 against bands of 0.737-0.831 and 1.871-2.110) and the omitted loading control (1.988), answering the earlier reviewer's recomputation complaint. But two tasks admit the claim's most emphasized error: in g2 raw unnormalized LDHA ratios (1.9021, 2.5476) sit 0.5% and 1.4% from the expected values inside an 8 percent band, and in g4 raw BAX ratios average 2.0715 against an expected 2.1242 inside a 6 percent band, so a subject who never normalizes passes both tasks outright. g5's job supplies S28's order of operations and names both aggregation procedures, so it measures execution rather than the judgment the claim asserts. Following the sections literally on each file does not produce a different number from the reference anywhere I could construct - the one ambiguity, subtracting a per-pixel background without multiplying by band area, is caught by g3's tolerance - so I list no hidden departure.

Criterion 4 (stronger grade passed over): A is the top grade the ladder offers, so the question is whether the stronger route inside A - quoting lane densities and the derived fold change from a deposited dataset - was genuinely pursued. python_checked.search_record shows 7 searches and 15 fetches, none of the searches logged for this claim and only 2 fetches for it; the justification's claim that searches for deposited lane-level densitometry and for saturation/linear-range criteria were run is borne out by two queries logged for other claims ('published western blot raw densitometry band intensity table supplementary data with reported fold change' and one ending 'linear dynamic range saturation threshold'), so the description is not inflated, but the effort aimed at this claim specifically was thin and the conclusion that no such paired dataset exists rests on incidental searching.

Criterion 5 (prior objections): the aggregation-order objection is answered by adding g5, whose per-membrane gains are correlated with the effect so the two orders differ by 19.9% for STAT3 and 0.5% for TUBB - though the new job hands the subject the correct order, so the pitfall is now tested as arithmetic rather than as judgment. The g3 tolerance objection is answered on substance (the uncorrected route now fails), but the justification repeats the same genus of error it was raised about: tolerance_basis states that leaving the background in gives 'about 0.70 and 1.73' for CDKN1A and CCND1, whereas the shipped bytes give 0.9192 and 1.7577. The g4 section-attribution objection is answered (S21 dropped from g4, g6 added to carry it). The g1 objection - that the job states the whole decision rule - is unchanged and acknowledged in uncertainty; it is mitigated by the fact that the stated rule is not one the sections supply. Of the earlier untested items, variability and aggregation order are now covered; SD/SE labelling, ROI and grid verification, n = 1 or 2, saved intermediates, visual cross-check and the laboratory remedies all remain untested and are acknowledged.
objections: g2's numeric fields do not bite on an omitted normalization: averaging the raw LDHA Treated/Normoxia ratios gives 1.9021 and 2.5476 against expected 1.8920 and 2.5840, inside the 8 percent band. The lane loading factor is only +/-8% and averages away over three repeats, so the claim's own rule 'Never plot raw intensities as a quantitative result' survives this task intact.

g4's mean_fold_usable_repeats does not bite on an omitted normalization either: raw BAX ratios of 2.1239, 2.3073 and 1.7832 average 2.0715, 2.5% from the expected 2.1242 and inside the 6 percent band, while the four structural fields are unaffected. The task's tolerance_basis considers only zero-imputation (1.59) and misses this route.

g5's job states S28's prescribed order of operations ('taking the ratio within each experiment first and then averaging') as the definition of the primary output and names both aggregation procedures, so it announces the planted issue and supplies the very judgment the claim asserts; what remains is arithmetic a subject with no knowledge of the skill could perform.

The justification's tolerance_basis for g3 states that leaving the background in gives 'about 0.70 and 1.73'; recomputed from the shipped bytes the GAPDH-normalized uncorrected folds are 0.9192 and 1.7577. The conclusion (both outside the 6 percent bands) survives, but this is the same class of arithmetic misstatement a prior reviewer flagged for this task.

Quote attachment is loose for several planted judgments: the single Eaton sentence about standards compensating for 'technical errors ... poor transfer or unequivocal loading' is used to underwrite g4's all_target_bands_detected, g6's casp3_high_variability and g6's most_discrepant_replicate, none of which it determines. Those outputs are determinate from the job's definitions, so they are not wrong, but the published rule is not doing the work the oracle_independence narrative claims.

No task scores a named corrective action, although expected_behavior makes 'names the prescribed remedy' half of the behavior under test; every output is a flag or a number, so a skill that detects defects but prescribes nothing would pass the whole suite.

g3's job narrates that the Control lane 'sits over a stain mark' and carries several times the background of the Treated lane. It reveals no output and restates a visible column, but it does pre-announce the defect, so the detection half of the claim is weakened even in the task that otherwise bites hardest.
required_revisions: Redesign g2 so an unnormalized analysis fails: make the per-lane loading factor large and correlated with condition (for example Hypoxia lanes loaded ~1.4x heavier), and state the LDHA fold request without embedding a per-total-protein quantity in the job, so the GAPDH-normalized, total-protein-normalized and unnormalized routes all separate under an 8 percent band.

Redesign g4 so the omitted loading-control normalization fails: give Treated lanes a systematically different load from Control lanes across repeats, so the raw mean fold falls well outside the 6 percent band while the normalized mean remains the expected value, keeping R3's missing BAX row as the planted defect.

Rewrite g5's job so it asks only for the treatment effect on each protein and whether the three membranes are poolable, without naming or describing either aggregation procedure, so that the subject must supply S28's order of operations rather than execute a dictated one.

Add at least one task that scores a prescribed remedy as a text or set field drawn from a fixed vocabulary (re-image at shorter exposure, dilute the lysate, switch to a total-protein stain, repeat the transfer, document the exclusion), so the 'names the remedy' half of expected_behavior is tested rather than assumed.

Attach quotes that actually underwrite the judgments they are filed against, or state plainly that those outputs rest on the job's arithmetic definition rather than on a published rule; the one Eaton sentence currently supporting three unrelated outputs in g4 and g6 should not be presented as the independent rule each follows.

Delete the sentence in g3's job identifying the Control lane as the high-background lane, leaving the asymmetry to be read off the local_background_per_px column, so the detection step is performed rather than announced.
coverage_gaps: S23/S28: the laboratory remedies the sections prescribe - re-image at a shorter exposure, dilute the lysate, repeat the transfer - are never scored, and no reference or logged search sought an oracle for a remedy vocabulary; a task could present a defective dataset and require a named corrective action from a fixed list.

S28: the skill's own saturation criterion (confirm max pixel value < 90% of detector range) is untested and untestable on these density tables; g1 substitutes a dilution-series proportionality rule supplied by the job. Eaton bears on the phenomenon but not on the pixel criterion.

S20/S28/S29.3: tuning lower_threshold and upper_threshold per image and verifying the grid overlay before extracting intensities is untested - defects are rows in a table rather than pixels - and the search record shows no query aimed at an image-level oracle.

S24/S28/S29.5: stating whether SD or SE is plotted and reporting n explicitly is untested; no task asks for an error measure at all, and the one logged query on SD versus SEM was made for another claim.
S28: drawing conclusions from n = 1 or n = 2 is untested as a flag; g3 is a single blot but its job asks only for folds and never whether the evidence supports a conclusion.

S29.6/S29.7: preserving raw intensities and ROI coordinates for re-analysis, and cross-checking the final chart against the qualitative impression of the blot, are untested and have no corresponding reference or search.

S21/S28: exclusion is tested only as 'report both analyses', which the job requires outright; no task requires the subject to justify or document an exclusion in its own words, so the documentation pitfall is covered only in reporting format.

outside_claim.reason: S28's saturated-loading-control pitfall and S22/S24's 'loading control bands are appropriate (not saturated)' check are exactly what a dilution series answers; the job supplies the arithmetic so a subject reading the sections cannot defensibly answer otherwise.

gives_away.reason: The job is symmetric over GAPDH and MDM2 and never says which antibody saturates; the rule it states (slope from the lowest load, 15 percent allowance) is not a rule the sections supply - S28's only saturation criterion is pixel-based (max pixel < 90% of detector range), which is inapplicable to a density table, so this belongs in criterion_given.

repeats.reason: No other task uses a load-response series or asks about proportionality to input.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed from the shipped bytes: slope 4993.6/ug; at 2.5/5/10 ug the ratios are 1.012/0.991/0.993 (inside 15%), at 20 ug 57313.2 against a predicted 99872 (43% low) and at 40 ug worse, so 10.0 and true; MDM2 is within 1% of its low-load slope at every point, so 40.0 and false. The Eaton quotes fairly state that saturation occurs within a load series and that a linear working range can span a wide load range.

wrong_passes.reason: The two booleans must split, so a constant answer fails; a 10% or 20% allowance returns the same two loads (the GAPDH deviation jumps from 1% to 43% between adjacent steps), and taking the slope from an all-points fit instead disqualifies every load and fails. I could not name an analysis that errs and still passes all four fields.

g1_dilution_series_linearity.criterion_given: Take the proportionality constant from the lowest load, allow 15 percent deviation, report the largest qualifying load.

outside_claim.reason: S28/S29.2 tell the analyst to check whether a housekeeping protein responds to the treatment and to prefer a total-protein stain; that is precisely what the job asks.

gives_away.reason: The job never says which housekeeping protein moves, and it does not state which denominator to use for the LDHA folds; the per-total-protein phrasing appears only inside the definitions of the two diagnostic booleans.

repeats.reason: No other task asks whether a reference protein is itself treatment-responsive.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: GAPDH per total protein falls from 0.05451 to 0.03265 (40% change, true); ACTB holds at 0.0583 vs 0.0581 (false); LDHA per total protein gives mean folds 1.8920 and 2.5840, matching the planted values.

wrong_passes.reason: Reporting raw LDHA ratios with no normalization at all - the claim's own flagship pitfall ('Never plot raw intensities as a quantitative result') - gives mean 1.9021 for 24h and 2.5476 for 48h against expected 1.8920 and 2.5840, i.e. 0.5% and 1.4% off, comfortably inside the 8 percent band, while the two booleans are computed exactly as the job dictates. The per-lane loading factor is only +/-8% and averages out over three repeats, so the task does not bite on an omitted normalization.

g2_treatment_responsive_control.criterion_given: More than 15 percent change per unit total protein between Hypoxia_48h and Normoxia counts as treatment-responsive.
g2_treatment_responsive_control.replacement: Keep the same three-repeat hypoxia panel but make the per-lane loading factor large and condition-correlated (for example Hypoxia lanes loaded roughly 1.4x heavier than Normoxia), and ask only for the amount of LDHA relative to Normoxia plus a judgment on each candidate reference, without the job specifying any per-total-protein quantity. Then the GAPDH-normalized answer, the ACTB/total-protein answer and the unnormalized answer all separate, so both the 'wrong reference' and the 'no reference' errors fail while the prescribed total-protein route passes.

outside_claim.reason: S23 tells the analyst to apply background subtraction using a local measurement near each band, and S28/S29.1 forbid reporting raw densities; the job asks for exactly the corrected, loading-normalized comparison and whether the raw comparison disagrees.

gives_away.reason: The sentence about the stain mark restates a value already visible in the local_background_per_px column (8.0 vs 2.0) and reveals no output: the job does not say which protein's raw comparison is misleading, does not say to normalize to GAPDH, and asks the disagreement question symmetrically for both proteins. The discriminating judgments - multiply background by band area, divide by the loading control - remain the subject's.

repeats.reason: It is the only task with a per-pixel background term and band areas, and the only two-lane single-blot case.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: corrected CDKN1A 11986.1/26656.5 = 0.44965 (Control) and 23829.4/67618.3 = 0.35241 (Treated), fold 0.78374; CCND1 fold 1.99070; raw CDKN1A rises 1.336x while the corrected fold falls, so disagree is true, and CCND1 rises on both readings, so false. All match the planted values; the Degasperi quotes state the per-band background removal and the per-lane normalization the outputs rest on.

wrong_passes.reason: Skipping the background term entirely gives 0.9192 and 1.7577 (expected bands 0.737-0.831 and 1.871-2.110) - both fail; subtracting the per-pixel value without area scaling gives essentially the same 0.919 and fails; skipping the loading control after correct background subtraction gives 1.988 for CDKN1A and fails and also flips its boolean. I could not name a wrong route that passes.

outside_claim.reason: S20 (bands not detected), S24 ('loading control bands present and measurable for all samples', 'all repetitions included') and S28's documentation pitfall all cover noticing and reporting an incomplete repeat rather than quantifying around it.

gives_away.reason: The field is defined with an explicit 'none if every repeat is complete' escape and no row, repeat or protein is named; the subject must find R3 and establish that the loading-control rows are all present.

repeats.reason: It is the only task where a measurement is absent from the file.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: R3 lacks Treated BAX, every GAPDH row is present, and the normalized folds for R1/R2/R4 are 2.0757, 2.4689 and 1.8278, mean 2.1242, with n=3 - all as planted.

wrong_passes.reason: Dropping the GAPDH normalization and averaging raw BAX Treated/Control ratios gives 2.1239, 2.3073 and 1.7832, mean 2.0715 - only 2.5% from the expected 2.1242 and inside the 6 percent band - while the four structural fields (R3, false, true, 3.0) are unaffected. The named pitfall 'reporting raw band intensities without loading-control normalization' therefore passes this task; the tolerance_basis considers only zero-imputation (1.59), not this route.

g4_incomplete_replicate.replacement: Keep the same four-repeat structure with R3's Treated BAX band absent, but make the per-lane loading systematically unequal between Control and Treated (for example Treated lanes carrying roughly 1.5x the load across repeats) so that the unnormalized mean fold lands far outside the tolerance while the GAPDH-normalized mean remains the expected value. The missing-band fields are unchanged and the task then bites on both the undetected band and the omitted normalization.

outside_claim.reason: S28 names this pitfall and S29 the remedy; the quantity asked for is within the claim.

gives_away.reason: The job spells out S28's prescribed order of steps verbatim in substance - 'computing the Treated-to-Control ratio inside each experiment and then averaging those three ratios' - and assigns it to the primary output field, and it announces that aggregation order is the issue under test by naming both procedures. The judgment the claim asserts (normalize within each replicate first, then aggregate) is handed to the subject, leaving only arithmetic; the 10 percent cut-off is additionally supplied.

repeats.reason: No other task contrasts two orders of aggregation.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: STAT3 per-repeat ratios 3.1602, 2.0157, 1.3498, mean 2.1752; pooling first gives 2.3514/1.3495 = 1.7424, 19.9% away, so true. TUBB ratios 1.7498, 1.8562, 1.8115, mean 1.8058; pooled 1.8147, 0.5% away, so false. All match the planted values.

wrong_passes.reason: Pooling first fails STAT3 (1.742 against a 2.045-2.306 band) and flips nothing else into agreement; the geometric mean of the ratios (2.049) is a defensible alternative rather than an error, and it sits at the edge of the band.

g5_aggregation_order.criterion_given: A disagreement of more than 10 percent between the two orders counts as the order mattering.
g5_aggregation_order.replacement: Ship the same three-membrane, two-protein file but ask only for the treatment effect on each protein (one fold per protein) and for a flag on whether the per-membrane scales make the experiments poolable, without naming or describing either aggregation procedure. Set the tolerance so that the pooled-first answer fails for STAT3 and both routes pass for TUBB; the subject then has to supply the order of operations from the claim rather than execute one the job dictated.

outside_claim.reason: S21 names large standard deviations between repetitions and conditional outlier exclusion, and S28/S29.4 require documenting rather than silently dropping; the job asks for the spread, the discrepant repeat and both analyses.

gives_away.reason: Neither the discrepant repeat nor which protein is variable is named, and the CV cut-off is not a threshold the sections state. Asking for both means is the sections' reporting remedy, but the detection work (which protein is variable, which repeat is discrepant) is left to the subject.

repeats.reason: It is the only task turning on inter-replicate spread; g4's defect is an absent row, not variability.

key_wrong.reason: Recomputed: CASP3 ratios 2.1811, 1.9322, 2.2403, 9.1749, 2.0428; CV 0.90 (true), median 2.1811 so R4 is furthest, mean all 3.5142, mean excluding 2.0991. HSP90 ratios 1.4419-1.6012, CV 0.04 (false). All planted values reproduce. The attached Eaton quotes are generic, but each of these outputs is fully defined computationally by the job, so no output depends on the quote to be determinate.

wrong_passes.reason: The two CV booleans must split; a population standard deviation gives CV 0.81, still true, and leaves everything else unchanged (not an error that passes while being wrong about anything scored); the two means differ by 40 percent, so neither can stand in for the other, and naming any repeat other than R4 fails.

findings: Criterion 1 (expected values right and skill-independent): I recomputed every output from the shipped bytes and all 26 planted values reproduce exactly - g1's 10.0/40.0 and the split booleans, g2's 1.8920/2.5840 with GAPDH down 40% per unit total protein and ACTB flat, g3's 0.78374/1.99070 with CDKN1A's raw comparison inverted, g4's R3/false/true/3.0/2.1242, g5's 2.1752/1.8058 with a 19.9% order effect for STAT3 and 0.5% for TUBB, and g6's CV 0.90/0.04, R4, 3.5142/2.0991. The generator implements the quoted Degasperi model (divide by a reference measured in the same sample) and nothing from the skill; every threshold used for scoring is stated in the job, not taken from the skill's text, and the reference solver derives each value from the files rather than reading arguments. Two weaknesses: several boolean and text outputs carry decorative quotes - one Eaton sentence about loading standards underwrites g4's undetected band, g6's CV flag and g6's discrepant repeat alike - so for those fields the rule actually in force is the job's arithmetic definition, not the published sentence; this does not make any value wrong but it thins the 'independent rule' story the justification tells.

Criterion 2 (exercising the claim as a whole): tested - saturated loading control (g1), treatment-responsive housekeeping protein (g2), raw/background-contaminated densities (g3), undetected band and incomplete repeat (g4), aggregation before fold change (g5), high inter-replicate variability and exclusion reporting (g6); each pairs its defect with a clean counterpart in the same file and each boolean pair must split, which is a real strength. Untested: naming any prescribed remedy (re-image, dilute, repeat the transfer, switch to a total-protein stain) although expected_behavior makes that half the behavior; the skill's own saturation criterion (max pixel < 90% of detector range, S28), which cannot be applied to a density table at all; ROI placement, grid-overlay verification and per-image threshold tuning (S20, S28, S29.3); stating SD vs SE and n (S24, S28, S29.5); drawing conclusions from n = 1 or 2 (S28); preserving intermediates and cross-checking the chart against the blot (S29.6-.7). Eaton bears on saturation and on housekeeping instability, so those gaps are covered by references; nothing in references or in python_checked.search_record bears on remedies, error-bar labelling or ROI work, and the record shows zero searches run for this claim in this attempt.

Criterion 3 (fair and searching comparison): g1, g3 and g6 bite properly - g3 in particular now rejects both the omitted background term (0.9192 and 1.7577 against bands of 0.737-0.831 and 1.871-2.110) and the omitted loading control (1.988), answering the earlier reviewer's recomputation complaint. But two tasks admit the claim's most emphasized error: in g2 raw unnormalized LDHA ratios (1.9021, 2.5476) sit 0.5% and 1.4% from the expected values inside an 8 percent band, and in g4 raw BAX ratios average 2.0715 against an expected 2.1242 inside a 6 percent band, so a subject who never normalizes passes both tasks outright. g5's job supplies S28's order of operations and names both aggregation procedures, so it measures execution rather than the judgment the claim asserts. Following the sections literally on each file does not produce a different number from the reference anywhere I could construct - the one ambiguity, subtracting a per-pixel background without multiplying by band area, is caught by g3's tolerance - so I list no hidden departure.

Criterion 4 (stronger grade passed over): A is the top grade the ladder offers, so the question is whether the stronger route inside A - quoting lane densities and the derived fold change from a deposited dataset - was genuinely pursued. python_checked.search_record shows 7 searches and 15 fetches, none of the searches logged for this claim and only 2 fetches for it; the justification's claim that searches for deposited lane-level densitometry and for saturation/linear-range criteria were run is borne out by two queries logged for other claims ('published western blot raw densitometry band intensity table supplementary data with reported fold change' and one ending 'linear dynamic range saturation threshold'), so the description is not inflated, but the effort aimed at this claim specifically was thin and the conclusion that no such paired dataset exists rests on incidental searching.

Criterion 5 (prior objections): the aggregation-order objection is answered by adding g5, whose per-membrane gains are correlated with the effect so the two orders differ by 19.9% for STAT3 and 0.5% for TUBB - though the new job hands the subject the correct order, so the pitfall is now tested as arithmetic rather than as judgment. The g3 tolerance objection is answered on substance (the uncorrected route now fails), but the justification repeats the same genus of error it was raised about: tolerance_basis states that leaving the background in gives 'about 0.70 and 1.73' for CDKN1A and CCND1, whereas the shipped bytes give 0.9192 and 1.7577. The g4 section-attribution objection is answered (S21 dropped from g4, g6 added to carry it). The g1 objection - that the job states the whole decision rule - is unchanged and acknowledged in uncertainty; it is mitigated by the fact that the stated rule is not one the sections supply. Of the earlier untested items, variability and aggregation order are now covered; SD/SE labelling, ROI and grid verification, n = 1 or 2, saved intermediates, visual cross-check and the laboratory remedies all remain untested and are acknowledged.

coverage_gaps: S23/S28: the laboratory remedies the sections prescribe - re-image at a shorter exposure, dilute the lysate, repeat the transfer - are never scored, and no reference or logged search sought an oracle for a remedy vocabulary; a task could present a defective dataset and require a named corrective action from a fixed list.

S28: the skill's own saturation criterion (confirm max pixel value < 90% of detector range) is untested and untestable on these density tables; g1 substitutes a dilution-series proportionality rule supplied by the job. Eaton bears on the phenomenon but not on the pixel criterion.

S20/S28/S29.3: tuning lower_threshold and upper_threshold per image and verifying the grid overlay before extracting intensities is untested - defects are rows in a table rather than pixels - and the search record shows no query aimed at an image-level oracle.

S24/S28/S29.5: stating whether SD or SE is plotted and reporting n explicitly is untested; no task asks for an error measure at all, and the one logged query on SD versus SEM was made for another claim.
S28: drawing conclusions from n = 1 or n = 2 is untested as a flag; g3 is a single blot but its job asks only for folds and never whether the evidence supports a conclusion.

S29.6/S29.7: preserving raw intensities and ROI coordinates for re-analysis, and cross-checking the final chart against the qualitative impression of the blot, are untested and have no corresponding reference or search.

S21/S28: exclusion is tested only as 'report both analyses', which the job requires outright; no task requires the subject to justify or document an exclusion in its own words, so the documentation pitfall is covered only in reporting format.
